problem: zeta(-n) = -B_{n+1}/(n+1) is stated without a range; with the usual convention B_1 = -1/2 it gives zeta(0) = +1/2, but zeta(0) = -1/2. It holds for n >= 1.

Perron's formula is stated with no conditions. It needs c > max(0, sigma_a), the integral exists only as a symmetric limit, and when x is an integer the last term must be halved, so as written it fails at integer x.
corrected: \sum_{n \le x} a_n = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{c - i\infty}^{c+i\infty} \Bigl(\sum_n \frac{a_n}{n^s}\Bigr) \frac{x^s}{s}\, ds \qquad (c > \max(0,\sigma_a),\ x \notin \mathbb Z)
